text: Refactoring is the process of improving the structure of your code without changing what it does. Think of it like cleaning and reorganizing a messy room: the furniture is still there, but it’s arranged better. The main goal is to make the code more readable and easier to maintain. This often means breaking long functions into smaller ones, renaming unclear variables, or removing duplicated code. By doing this regularly, you reduce "technical debt"—the hidden cost of messy code that makes future changes slow and risky. While refactoring takes time, it pays off by making your codebase cleaner and your team more productive.
